A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, despite the COG-to-LOL renaming and revised title. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original normality-testing experiments, ImageNet interpolation and centroid comparisons, and image and point-cloud subspace demonstrations.

after.justification: v5 retains those quantitative experiments and reports a revised 3D subspace demonstration with original aircraft wave-drag simulations.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming COG to LOL, v5 Appendix A introduces a procedure for distributions with independent coordinates and known marginal CDFs and inverses: Gaussianize each seed, combine and normalize, then transform back. The original Gaussian correction and subspace construction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: ImageNet1k and ShapeNet remain the datasets used. Figure 7 replaces the mixed-object point-cloud demonstration with aircraft meshes and simulated wave-drag evaluation, adding a physical-design scenario within the existing 3D coverage. The non-Gaussian extension is not empirically evaluated.

E2.justification: The interpolation comparators remain LERP, SLERP, and NAO; centroid comparators remain Euclidean, standardized Euclidean, mode-norm Euclidean, and NAO. Table 2 also retains the same normality-test comparators. DDMI and SLIDE are demonstration models, not competing manipulation methods.

E3.justification: The Figure 7 demonstration changes from DDMI with a six-dimensional subspace to SLIDE with a three-dimensional subspace, displaying a 10-by-10 design grid and evaluating wave drag over a 100-by-100 grid. The ImageNet sampling, 400-step inversion/generation settings, guidance scale, and comparison metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The revised Figure 7 case study examines variation of a simulated physical objective across a latent subspace, extending the earlier visual demonstration of model-independent subspace construction. Existing inversion-budget ablations, normality failure cases, uncorrected subspaces, and large-centroid failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same 10,000-sample normality-test reporting, percentile summaries, and 99% intervals for the SLERP approximation. Figure 4 replaces acceptance percentages with complementary rejection percentages without introducing a new statistical procedure or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Figure 7 replaces the DDMI point-cloud results with SLIDE aircraft designs and a wave-drag landscape. Numerical entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged, including interpolation accuracy/FID of 67.4%/38.9 and centroid accuracy/FID of 46.3%/87.7 for the proposed method.

T1.justification: v5 Appendix A adds the independent-coordinate distributional construction, a distribution-preservation proof, and a claimed Monge-optimality proof. Appendix B adds quadratic optimal-transport reasoning for the Gaussian correction. The earlier Gaussian-preservation, SLERP-approximation, and subspace-weight proofs are retained and renumbered.

C1.justification: v5 broadens the principal applicability claim from Gaussian latents to a general class of latent distributions and elevates Monge optimality to a main contribution. The abstract removes its explicit interpolation-outperformance sentence and foregrounds subspaces; the performance claim remains in Section 5.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly interprets simulated objectives over latent subspaces as enabling design optimization, although no optimization run is reported. The distribution-testing discussion emphasizes diagnosing inversion settings, and the conclusion explicitly notes that tests may be stricter than a network requires.

D1.justification: v5 identifies authors-trained SLIDE on ShapeNet, mesh reconstruction, and OpenVSP as the simulation implementation for the revised 3D example. The detailed DDIM, NAO, classifier, and FID implementation information for the retained experiments is unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds references for SLIDE, OpenVSP, and computational optimal transport, while removing the DDMI reference. It also drops v4's statement that normality testing had not been seen in generative-model literature. The broader related-work discussion remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: COG becomes LOL, with revised title, abstract, contribution wording, authorship, and publication header. Section 3 is reorganized, normality-test details move to Appendix E, and related-work subsections become run-in headings. The overall section sequence and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 exchange order, Figure 4 changes its acceptance/rejection display, and Figure 7 replaces point-cloud grids with aircraft designs and a wave-drag heatmap. Captions and figure placement are revised, and appendix material is repaginated; most illustrations and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 strengthens the Gaussian correction's rationale with an optimal-transport derivation and demonstrates a more concrete application through aircraft wave-drag evaluation. These provide a limited overall gain. Benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the general extension remains theoretical; its optimality proof operates on Gaussianized sums, leaving the guarantee for original non-Gaussian linear combinations less clearly established.
